quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: concerns about the Clippers' roster and potential franchise reset
quotes.excerpt: the Clippers are going through or trying to get to a pretty major franchise reset
quotes.quote: The Clippers are going through or trying to get to a pretty major franchise reset that is obviously not about winning right now, but about moving past a pretty tough chapter in franchise history, just because the expectations were so high and the payoff was not much. They are somewhere in the 30-ish win range and the Clippers are trying to get to a pretty major franchise reset.

quotes.speaker: Ben McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Chet Holmgren's health is key to the Thunder's win total
quotes.excerpt: this comes down so much to can Jalen Williams, J-Dub stay healthy
quotes.quote: I am an over and I do think that they are a significantly thinner team. They do not have the depth that they had last year just because they did lose three quality role players, one of whom was a starter. But they were a 68-win team a couple years ago, they were a 64-win team last year. I guess you could say if that trend holds up they are a 60-win team this year. But really to me, this comes down so much to can Jalen Williams, J-Dub stay healthy. They won 64 games last year and he played like 33 of them. I know he is working awfully hard on his body this summer to do everything within his power to position himself to be durable this year.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Cason Wallace and Jalen Williams' expanded roles for the Thunder
quotes.excerpt: Ajay Mitchell's role is going to be bigger, Cason Wallace's role is going to be bigger
quotes.quote: Ajay Mitchell's role is going to be bigger. Cason Wallace's role is going to be bigger. Jared McCain's role is going to be bigger. They had these guys who were mostly out last year, Thomas Sorber, and then they drafted these guys, Adai Mara and Bennett Sturtz. I do not know, maybe they have a role. So I also feel good about that being over, despite the challenges in the West.

quotes.speaker: Ben McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs' young core development
quotes.excerpt: Wemby is just at the launching point. Stefan Castle is launching. Dylan Harper is going to end up
quotes.quote: You talk about ascending talent, Wemby is just at the launching point. Stefan Castle is launching. Dylan Harper I think is going to end up being their second best player, maybe as soon as this year. You could certainly argue that he was in the finals. So their core, they could have three all-NBA caliber players as soon as this season. I think obviously Wemby is the MVP front-runner. Stefan Castle is going to be in the all-NBA conversation if he can stay healthy and keep his trajectory. It might be a little early for Harper, but he is on his way.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Cam Johnson's struggles in a new system
quotes.excerpt: Cam Johnson had a bad year last year, and I think in large part because he was playing
quotes.quote: Cam Johnson had a bad year last year, and I think in large part because he was playing in a system they had never played in before. And I think it affected him.

quotes.speaker: Ben McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Peyton Watson's contract and role with the Nuggets
quotes.excerpt: there is a huge question mark here, which is will Peyton Watson be on their roster
quotes.quote: There is a huge question mark here, which is will Peyton Watson be on their roster. He had a great month that he is hoping to cash in on. And it is looking very uncertain at this point. There are certainly other teams that are interested. His asking price of basically Christian Brown's contract, I do not think he gets that. I will also believe that he plays for the qualifying offer when I see it.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen McDaniels' potential leap and extension eligibility
quotes.excerpt: is Jalen McDaniels about to take a leap after the way he played in the playoffs
quotes.quote: Is Jalen McDaniels about to take a leap after the way he played in the playoffs last year? Is this role, them clearing out some stuff for him, is this -- by the way, he is extension eligible. So that is something to keep a little eye on. Is he about to leap forward into being an All-Star?

quotes.speaker: Ben McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: the Blazers' organizational dysfunction and coaching challenges
quotes.excerpt: the whole franchise is a complete mess right now because of all the stuff happening with the arena
quotes.quote: I've got chemistry concerns, I've got organizational concerns. I think the whole franchise is a complete mess right now because of all the stuff happening with the arena, the relocation, the owner being a total cheap ass, the coach coming in with handcuffs on because the owner is such a cheap ass and the way that the contract was done. I just think there's too much mess around the Blazers right now for them to be a playoff team. John and Dame is your starting backcourt. Man, Donovan Clingan better be one hell of an elite defender too.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: the Rockets' fourth-quarter struggles and turnover issues
quotes.excerpt: they were eighth in offense last season despite being a horrible fourth-quarter team
quotes.quote: Remember they were eighth in offense last season despite being a horrible fourth-quarter team. They were bottom five in turnovers and bottom ten in assists, and in the fourth quarters they were almost worse. Look, I'm still not 100% convinced of the Durant fit, but I am convinced of Durant's still ability to be a game-changing player.

quotes.speaker: Ben McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: the Lakers' long-term strategy around Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves
quotes.excerpt: what they were trying to do was put a long-term core in place around Luka and Austin Reaves
quotes.quote: What they were trying to do was put a long-term core in place around Luka and Austin Reaves, and to do that, you couldn't have LeBron making a bunch of money. Now, why didn't LeBron take the minimum from the Lakers? That's a whole different story. Point being, I understand why they were prepared to move on from LeBron, okay? Because it's their future is more important than LeBron right now, but LeBron was a massive contributor to that team last year.
